column1: # Findings the harness MUST still find, and must still report.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Every other gate in this project asks "did anything go
# wrong". None of them asks "would we have noticed if it had". A sweep that
# builds, fuzzes for twenty minutes, gates cleanly and ships a report proves
# the pipeline RAN -- it proves nothing whatever about whether the pipeline can
# still SEE. A harness that silently stopped parsing UBSan output, or stopped
# carrying parsed sites into the census, would pass every check on the board
# and go on passing them forever.
# So this is the positive control, and it fails in the opposite direction from
# everything else here: absence is the failure. The project's rule that
# "absence is never a pass" is usually about not reading silence as health;
# this is the same rule pointed at the instrument instead of the subject.
# NOT A LIST OF BUGS TO FIX. These are recorded findings that a short run
# reaches reliably. They are here because they are DEPENDABLE, not because they
# are important -- a defect that fires once a week is a fine finding and a
# useless canary. Fixing one upstream is not a problem: withdraw the row, in a
# commit that says the fix landed.
# BUILT FROM OBSERVATION, NOT FROM THE ACCEPT-LIST, and rebuilt once the first
# version was wrong. Every row below appeared in ALL SIX 16/17 undefined
# records now on hand, from THREE separate GitHub runs (33891551739,
# ONE OBSERVATION IS NOT REPRODUCIBILITY. The first version of this file was
# built from a single run and asserted isoweek2j, which appeared in five of the
# six records and not in the sixth -- so the control failed a healthy run, and
# was right to: the row was not dependable and the list said it was. It is
# withdrawn. A row that fires most of the time is a fine finding and a useless
# canary, which is the whole distinction this file exists to make.
# AND pg_strtoint64_safe IS BACK. The first version excluded it with the note
# "did not fire once in either run". That was a measurement error, not a fact:
# the extraction used to build the list missed its frame. It is present in all
# six records. Recorded here because the mistake is instructive -- the list is
# only as good as the query that produced it, and "absent" needed checking
# twice as hard as "present".
# KEYED ON FUNCTION, NOT LINE. timestamp.c:1945 on 16 is timestamp.c:2016 on
# 17. The function survives a rebase; the line does not.
# TWO ASSERTIONS PER ROW, because "found" and "reported" are different claims:
#   found     the function is the innermost frame of a UB report in the logs
#   reported  the census turned that log into a signature naming the file
# The first can pass while the second fails -- that is exactly the regression
# where parsing still works and the reporting layer has quietly come loose.
# "reported" is file-level because the census keys signatures on file:line,
# which is why the file column is here rather than being derivable.
# scope is a comma-separated list of workspace-name globs, as in
# scripts/ubsan-baseline.tsv, and the star may appear anywhere.
# THE SANITIZER IS PART OF THE SCOPE. A UBSan site cannot fire in an ASan
# build, so "ci-rel_16*" was wrong -- it matched ci-rel_16_stable-address and
# asserted seven findings against a run that could not physically produce one.
# The first draft of this file did exactly that and the control failed 7 of 7
# on a healthy workspace, which is the right failure for the wrong reason.
# 18+ has no rows yet: those builds have never completed a sweep, so there is
# no observation to base one on, and a guess here would defeat the purpose of
# the file.
